title: Launch-week monitoring + rate-limit guardrails for public benchmark landing page
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Context
The benchmark report launch is expected to drive bursty traffic to the public landing page and interactive table (JSON results feed). We need launch-week observability, alerting, and guardrails (rate limits + cache protections) to avoid: (a) marketing site latency/timeouts, (b) cache miss storms, (c) runaway origin load on the benchmark results service, (d) elevated 429s/5xx that degrade the public narrative.

Goals
- Ship a launch dashboard for real-time monitoring (site + results feed + CDN).
- Add pragmatic guardrails: rate limits, circuit breakers, and caching defaults that survive traffic spikes.
- Define an on-call / escalation path + runbook for launch day.
- Validate via pre-launch load test and a controlled cache-warm workflow.

Non-goals
- Re-architect the results service (keep changes minimal; we can iterate after launch).
- “Perfect” DDoS protection beyond existing WAF/CDN (just ensure sane config + visibility).

Success criteria / acceptance
1) Dashboards
- Single “Launch: Benchmark Page” dashboard covering:
  - Marketing site p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, and top routes
  - Benchmark results JSON endpoint: RPS, p95 latency, 4xx/5xx breakdown, cache hit ratio
  - CDN metrics: cache hit %, origin fetch rate, origin errors
  - Backend: CPU/mem for results service, upstream storage latency
  - User journey funnel events (CTA clicks) for sanity checks during peak (best-effort visibility only)

2) Alerts (paging for Sev2+ only)
- Page on: sustained 5xx on benchmark results endpoint, sustained elevated origin latency, and cache hit ratio collapse.
- Non-paging alerts: elevated 429s, elevated marketing-site TTFB, spikes in origin fetches.
- Alert thresholds documented in the runbook.

3) Guardrails
- Confirm CDN cache TTL and stale-while-revalidate for benchmark artifact JSON.
- Add per-IP + global rate limit on the results endpoint (protect origin, avoid making page unusable).
- Add an emergency “static snapshot” fallback path (manual toggle) if the results service is unhealthy.
- Ensure cache warming procedure is documented and tested.

4) Operational readiness
- Runbook includes:
  - How to interpret dashboards
  - Fast mitigations (raise cache TTL, enable serve-stale, temporarily tighten rate limits)
  - Comms template for Marketing/Support
  - Escalation chain (Eng oncall, Web, Infra)

Implementation plan (high level)
A) Monitoring / dashboards (Datadog + CDN console)
- Create dedicated dashboard: “Launch: Benchmark report (public)”
- Add golden signals and top endpoints:
  - GET /benchmarks (landing)
  - GET /benchmarks/data/v* (JSON artifacts)
  - GET /assets/* (PDF + figures)
- Add synthetic checks for the landing page and JSON feed from 3 regions (NA/EU/APAC).

B) Alerting
- Results endpoint:
  - 5xx rate > 1% for 5m (page)
  - p95 latency > 2s for 10m (page)
  - cache hit ratio < 70% for 10m (page)
- Marketing site:
  - p95 TTFB > 1.5s for 10m (slack)
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10m (slack)
- CDN/origin protection:
  - origin fetch rate spike (> 3x baseline for 10m) (slack)

C) Guardrails
- CDN:
  - Default TTL: 10m for versioned JSON artifacts (v1, v2, …)
  - Enable serve-stale: 60m
  - Ensure content is immutable once versioned; do not overwrite artifacts.
- Results service:
  - Per-IP rate limit (soft) and global concurrency cap
  - Return 304 aggressively on If-None-Match/ETag
  - Ensure responses are cacheable with strong ETags
- Fallback:
  - Manual flag to serve last-known-good artifact directly from object storage (bypass compute) if service unhealthy

D) Launch day operations
- Owner: Sean (SRE)
- Backup: Neha (Reliability), Logan (Telemetry)
- “War room” Slack channel + checklist for launch window.

Notes / risks
- Biggest risk is cache miss storm on first-wave traffic (social/email blast) if CDN config is wrong or artifacts are not warmed.
- Need to align with Legal/PMM that any “fallback snapshot” is acceptable as long as the artifact version is published and consistent.

Links
- Related: ENG-18566 (benchmark results service & cache layer)
- Related: ENG-18477 (artifact export pipeline to web)
- Product: PM-826 (interactive benchmark page requirements + analytics)
- Docs PR (for landing page disclaimers): redwood-docs PR-3912 (reference)
comments: 2025-06-27 (Sean Gallagher): Creating this as a hard launch blocker. We’ve seen similar patterns on prior announcements: CDN hit ratio starts low -> origin thunders. We need serve-stale + cache warming before the first email blast.

2025-06-28 (Logan Wright): Telemetry note: we can pipe page interaction events (filter changes/export/click CTA) into the same launch dashboard as a “sanity” panel. Not for paging, but useful to correlate load with conversions. Instrumentation work is in PR-27905; should land before July 5.

2025-06-30 (Vanessa Ortiz): Capacity reservation for inference regions is separate, but FYI: marketing traffic should not touch inference fleet directly. Only risk is results service + CDN. Please confirm results endpoint is isolated and has autoscaling enabled.

2025-07-01 (Felix Schneider): For the interactive table, the UI currently fetches JSON on page load + on filter changes. I can debounce filter requests and ensure the UI doesn’t spam the endpoint (especially on mobile). Will add a client-side guard (min 300ms debounce) and rely on ETags.

2025-07-02 (Neha Kapoor): Alert thresholds look reasonable. Please ensure paging is only for sustained issues; do not page on single-point spikes during the first 2 minutes of launch. Also add a playbook step: “tighten rate limit if origin is threatened” vs “loosen if too many legit users are blocked.”

2025-07-03 (Sean Gallagher): Dashboard draft is up in Datadog: “Launch: Benchmark report (public)”. Added panels for 200/304/429/5xx split, origin latency, CDN hit ratio. Still missing synthetic checks from EU/APAC; waiting on creds for external probes.

2025-07-05 (Sean Gallagher): Implemented CDN defaults (TTL 10m, serve-stale 60m) for versioned JSON + PDF assets. Added runbook section on artifact immutability: publish a new version instead of overwriting. Coordinating with PMM so we don’t ‘hot edit’ v1 after launch without bumping version.

2025-07-06 (Omar El-Sayed): Results service p95 latency spikes correlate with cache misses on cold start. Recommend pre-warm by fetching the top 10 JSON artifacts per region prior to the launch blast (and after deploy). Added a simple curl warm script to the runbook.

2025-07-07 (Sean Gallagher): Load test (k6) against /benchmarks/data/v1.json at 200 RPS shows stable p95 < 400ms with CDN warm; with cold cache, origin spikes and p95 > 2.5s. We need to bake cache warm into the launch checklist and post-deploy hook.

2025-07-08 (Launch day, Sean Gallagher): War room open 08:00–12:00 PT. Cache warmed at 07:50 PT. Monitoring dashboards shared in #marketing and #eng-sre. Rate limits enabled: per-IP 60 req/min burst 120; global concurrency cap 500. No issues observed during first email blast.

2025-07-09 (Sean Gallagher): Noted a short-lived spike in 429s (~3 minutes) following a partner newsletter blast. Mitigation: increased per-IP burst to 180 while keeping sustained limit, and confirmed CDN hit ratio stayed >90%. Added note to runbook: prefer raising burst before raising sustained limits.

2025-07-10 (Sean Gallagher): Minor incident: cache miss storm after a config push invalidated a subset of CDN keys; origin latency jumped; landing page partially degraded. Serve-stale prevented full outage, but interactive table felt slow for ~6 minutes. Action item created: lock down cache config changes during launch windows + add ‘cache hit ratio collapse’ paging threshold (done).

2025-07-17 (Sean Gallagher): Closing ticket post-launch. Dashboards + alerts remained in place through launch week; runbook updated with incident learnings. Follow-ups filed: (1) automate cache warm as part of deploy, (2) better segmented rate limits (bots vs humans), (3) add status banner in UI when results endpoint returns stale data.
